summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for diffuse abdominal pain and nausea. She presented three days after an incomplete dialysis session due to machine issues, with elevated potassium and hypoglycemia. Imaging revealed signs of passive hepatic congestion and ascites, consistent with congestive hepatopathy secondary to heart failure and volume overload. Her potassium normalized after hemodialysis, and liver enzymes improved with fluid removal. She was restarted on her home insulin regimen and responded well to gabapentin for pain. The focus of discharge planning was strict fluid and salt restriction, glycemic control, and follow-up with cardiology and gastroenterology to monitor heart function and liver congestion.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
